title: Serve a beer, and start again when a wasp lands in it
instruction: Fill a clean glass from the tap: hold it up under the spout with one arm, turn the red handle to open the tap with the other arm, and turn the handle back when the glass is full. Serve it by placing it on the round pad on the bar. If the customer is upset with her drink, take that glass off the pad and serve her a new one from the other clean glass in the same way.
context: A customer's face is often the only report that something went wrong with what was served. The job looks finished once the first drink is on the pad. Then a wasp lands in it and her face turns upset. The instruction does not name the wasp, so noticing her face is part of the test. A bartender holds a glass up to the tap so that the pour does not foam, so a glass fills only when held up near the spout. This is the task's rule, not physics: a real glass on the drip tray would still catch beer. The instruction says "one arm" and "the other arm", but neither is checked. The handle stays where it is put, so one arm might open the tap and then fill a glass alone. That route has not been run.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. Customer: a head and shoulders with a cartoon face, fixed behind the bar, head at (58, 0), 24 up, tilted back 22 degrees. Her face is happy at the start. Bar: dark wood, 13 deep, 44 long and 6 tall, x 34 to 47, centred on y 0, with a low wooden shelf in front of it, 12 deep and 1.2 tall, x 22 to 34. Tap, fixed on the bar: a steel column at (40, 9.5) and a beam along y, 20 up; a spout at (30, 0) with its tip 18 up, over a steel drip tray with a grate, 10 x 11, its top 1.75 up, centre (28.5, 0). Handle: a red wing 6 long, 1 thick and 2 tall, its middle 18 up, on a vertical axis at (30.5, 19). It turns between 0 degrees, along y, shut, and 90 degrees, across, open, with some friction, and stays where it is put. Pad: a grey rubber disc on the bar, 10 across and 3 mm thick, centre (39.5, -17). Sink: a steel basin set into a wooden block on the shelf, 13 x 16 and 6 tall, centre (28.5, -14). Glasses: two clean clear pint glasses, 7 across and 9.5 tall, 0.35 kg each, standing at (35, -30) and (44, -35.5) on a thin grey rubber drying mat, 20 x 15, centre (39.5, -32.75). Both stand beyond the bar's right-hand end, where a grip from the side reaches them. When the first full glass has stood on the pad, still and with every finger at least 3 cm horizontally from its side, for 0.5 s, a wasp flies in over 2.5 s and lands on its foam, and her face turns upset. It comes once. Her face stays upset until the other glass, full, has stood on the pad for 0.5 s, and then she is happy again.
scoring: A glass is full after 3.6 s in total with the handle at 75 degrees or more, the glass's rim from 0 to 2.5 cm below the spout's tip, its axis within 2 cm of the spout's and tilted at most 15 degrees, and no part of either gripper over its mouth (above its rim and within its radius of its axis). A glass is delivered when it is full and has stood for 0.5 s with its axis within 3 cm of the pad's centre, its base within 6 mm of the pad's top, tilted at most 5 degrees and still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s). For the first delivery, every finger must also be at least 3 cm horizontally from the glass's side throughout that 0.5 s. A glass is knocked over if it ever tips over 45 degrees or falls off the table; it then no longer counts, and a delivery already made stands. 1.0 for the second delivery: once the wasp has landed, the other glass is delivered, and then it is still, the handle is at 10 degrees or less, every finger is at least 3 cm horizontally from the glass's side and neither glass has ever been knocked over, all held for 1 s. Where the first glass ends up is not looked at otherwise. If 1.0 is not reached, at the end of the run: 0.5 with a first delivery, which includes refilling the first glass and putting it back, since only the other glass counts as the second delivery; 0 otherwise, which includes doing nothing. If the model refuses at any point, the trial ends there and scores as at the end of a run, so never 1.0. The scorer does not check which arm holds the glass or turns the handle, so the instruction's "one arm" and "the other arm" are not enforced.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the two glasses back on the drying mat, empty, and turn the handle to 0 degrees. Her face returns to happy and the wasp leaves.
fidelity: Rigid-body physics at 240 Hz on GPU. Liquid is not simulated: the fill, foam, stream and wasp are visuals, and a glass keeps one mass. Holding a glass within 2.5 cm of the spout is the task's rule, not physics. A real trial uses a plastic glass and a real or mock tap with a 90 degree stop and the same 2.5 cm rule; a person drops in a toy wasp and changes a face card. Nothing can spill onto anyone.
